title: STILL PRESENT (r2): Queued-row take-over can never be confirmed — W6 added the menu entry but the Queued row detail never renders the take-over confirm
location: client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam — overflow_actions Queued arm vs row_detail Queued arm
evidence:
+    Queued ->
+      list.append([RefcheckStart, RefcheckSkip], case call.hooks.can_take_over {
+        True -> [RefcheckTakeOver]
+        False -> []
+      })
...
     Queued ->
+      html.div([class("space-y-3")], [
+        html.p([class("text-sm text-slate leading-relaxed")], [
+          html.text(copy.refcheck_state_queued),
+        ]),
+        case
+          pending_confirm(call.reference_call_id, RefcheckConfirmStart, confirm)
+        {
+          True -> view_start_confirm(call, app, slot, inflight)
+          False -> element.none()
+        },
+      ])
detail: r2 W6 made Queued rows offer 'Take over manually', but view_take_over_confirm renders only in the Unreachable and ContactInitiated arms. Choosing take-over on a Queued row sets refcheck_confirm to a state nothing renders; the action is unconfirmable dead UI.
recommended_fix: Add the RefcheckConfirmTakeOver pending_confirm branch to the Queued arm of row_detail (mirroring Unreachable/ContactInitiated) so the §7.7 confirm renders, or gate take-over out of the Queued menu.

title: Successful action response clears refcheck_edit/refcheck_confirm unconditionally — an unrelated row's open edit trio is wiped, losing typed referee PII
evidence:
+            Ok(_) -> {
+              let cleared =
+                Model(
+                  ..model,
+                  refcheck_edit: None,
+                  refcheck_confirm: None,
+                  refcheck_action_inflight: set.delete(
+                    model.refcheck_action_inflight,
+                    call_id,
+                  ),
+                )
detail: Skip/re-enable on row B returns Ok while the landlord is mid-edit on row A's correction trio; the form is closed and typed values destroyed. A pending start/take-over confirm on another row is silently dismissed too. Failure path re-enables scoped to call_id; success path is unscoped.
recommended_fix: Clear refcheck_edit only when edit.call_id == call_id (and refcheck_confirm only when confirm.call_id == call_id), mirroring the failure path's scoped edit_reenabled guard.

title: AppCompletedRefcheckExport ignores its call_id — no staleness guard, so a slow clipboard write settling after navigation still toasts on the wrong page
evidence:
+    AppCompletedRefcheckExport(_call_id, result) ->
+      case result {
+        Ok(_) ->
+          add_toast(
+            Model(..model, clipboard_copied: None),
+            copy.refcheck_toast_exported,
+            ToastSuccess,
+          )
+        Error(_) ->
+          add_toast(
+            Model(..model, clipboard_copied: None),
+            copy.refcheck_toast_export_failed,
+            ToastError,
+          )
detail: The sibling report-download handler is described in the same diff as carrying an id-mismatch guard; this export handler binds _call_id and discards it. clipboard_copied is set to a sentinel but never compared, so it guards nothing.
recommended_fix: Drop the toast when the route no longer shows the call (reuse refcheck_response_is_current) or verify clipboard_copied still equals the sentinel before toasting.

title: Substitution's returned reference_call_id is decoded but never consumed — the handler discards the payload and keeps the old call_id
evidence:
+/// only payload the client needs is the substitution's new row id (absent
+/// -> ""). A successful HTTP round-trip is the signal; the detail refetch
+/// carries the real state.
+fn action_result_decoder() -> decode.Decoder(String) {
+  use id <- decode.optional_field(
+    "reference_call_id",
+    None,
+    decode.optional(decode.string),
+  )
+  decode.success(option.unwrap(id, ""))
+}
...
+            Ok(_) -> {
detail: The module contract says the response carries the substitution's new row id, but ApiReturnedRefcheckAction's Ok arm discards the String (Ok(_)) and the guard/toast run on the original call_id. The decoded value is dead plumbing.
recommended_fix: Consume the new id (e.g. expand the new row, or use it in the guard) or simplify the decoder to decode.success("") with the contract comment corrected.

title: no_em_dash_test checks the same character twice — "\u{2014}" and "—" are both U+2014
detail: The escape resolves at compile time, so both operands are the identical string; the second disjunct can never be the sole trigger and the check reads as covering two forms it doesn't.
recommended_fix: Drop the duplicate `string.contains(s, "—")` disjunct, or if two spellings were intended, differentiate them (e.g. also scan for a hyphen-minus pair).
